subject.title: [Feature]: Skill lifecycle management — auto-optimization on failure + usage-based retirement

question: Should failure-driven skill repair and usage-based skill retirement live in OpenClaw core, behind a new plugin/ClawHub API seam, or be declined for now?
rationale: The requested behavior changes how OpenClaw derives durable skill edits from agent failures and how it hides or deletes user skill artifacts, which expands product policy, storage, config, privacy, and safety boundaries beyond a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Split and design core seams first
options.body: Define the minimum core telemetry, proposal provenance, and restore-safe archive semantics needed, then let core or plugins build on that approved contract.

options.title: Route as plugin or ClawHub experiment
options.body: Keep core lean by exposing only missing extension points and asking lifecycle policy, ranking, and retirement behavior to live outside core until demand and safety are proven.

options.title: Decline lifecycle automation for now
options.body: Keep manual Skill Workshop curation plus existing correction capture and avoid automatic retirement/delete behavior until a stronger product case appears.

recommendation.title: Split and design core seams first
recommendation.body: Define the minimum core telemetry, proposal provenance, and restore-safe archive semantics needed, then let core or plugins build on that approved contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame and release-history evidence make Vincent Koc the strongest current owner for the Skill Research, config, and proposal-state surface that would need design changes.
